sentences.text: With the concurrence of learned counsel for the parties, the petition was heard finally and today the order is being pronounced.

2. This petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, Narsingpur vide Crime No.51/2022 on the fulcrum of a complaint made by respondent No.2 against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n),
328, 506, 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
It is also claimed that order framing charges dated 11.09.2023 passed by Second Additional Sessions Judge, Narsinghpur may also be quashed.

3. Succinct portrayal of facts is that the complainant lodged an FIR on 04.09.2022 at Mahila Thana Narsinghpur alleging therein that she resides at Kolar Road, Bhopal and the petitioner who being an Inspector in police station is posted as SHO PS Lalbagh Burhanpur and on 12.11.2017 the petitioner contacted her on mobile after arranging the number from matrimonial site wherein in his profile,
the petitioner's educational qualification and information about caste were incorrectly shown and he pretended himself to be a victim of wife, gained full sympathy from the complainant.
He first time on 30.11.2017 went to the rented house of prosecutrix at Panchwati Colony, Gadarwara and stayed there and also developed physical relations with complainant against her will.

Further, on 18.06.2018 when complainant took another house on rent at Near Kabra Memorial School,
Gadarwara, again the petitioner came and stayed in the house and developed physical relations with her.
She alleged that on the false pretext of marriage and after administering her sleeping-pills he developed physical relation.

The complainant got him appointed on the post of Principal in a private school and thereafter at the instant of complainant, the petitioner got appointed as Administrator in CBSE Senior Secondary School.
The petitioner used to visit her house oftentimes and physical relations were continued between them.

In the month of November, 2018 the complainant came to know about a crime registered against the petitioner vide Crime No.933/2018 at Police Station T.T.
Nagar, Bhopal then petitioner got dismissed from the post of Administrator.

The petitioner came back in police service on 30.09.2020 and then he came to her house at Burhanpur and stayed for eight days and during that period also, physical relations were developed between them.
After coming to know about the fact that against the petitioner criminal cases of rape, dacoity, etc. have also been registered then only she felt ashamed and cheated.

Thus, she made a complaint on 23.07.2022 to the police headquarters and thereafter the petitioner on 27.07.2022 made a complaint through his wife Sonali Singh and got the offence under Section 376 IPC registered against the complainant and her relatives.
It is alleged that said complaint was false as incident was said to have taken place on 05.11.2020 whereas on that date, complainant was at Bhopal.
The petitioner also made a false complaint against the complainant making allegation of blackmailing by demanding Rs.4 lakh from the petitioner.
Further, the brother of the complainant was assaulted by hooligans at the instance of petitioner.
One Deepshikha at the instance of petitioner also lodged false complaint against the complainant and her brother.

She alleged that she was under tremendous pressure and gave affidavit to the police for not lodging the FIR, but that was done at the instance of petitioner and as such she lodged the report that appropriate action be taken against the petitioner.
4. Pinpointing the demeanour of the complainant, learned counsel for the petitioner sanguinely submitted that the complainant is a married woman with Anurag Upadhyay and having a daughter Amitabh Pratap Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67308039/
2 20-year- old.

sentences.text: She never took divorce from her husband and still her status in her matrimonial profile is shown as 'married' and as such offence under Section 326(2)(n) of IPC is not made out against the petitioner because the Supreme Court has consistently observed that a married lady cannot be assured of marriage and on that assurance, physical relation if developed, offence under Section 376 IPC is not made out.

He submitted that the petitioner and complainant, both are married persons and they are well aware of this fact and therefore allegation made by the complainant that on the false pretext of marriage, the physical relations were developed by the petitioner, has no meaning in the eyes of law and as such no offence under Section 376 of IPC is made out.

Shri Kochar further submitted that the disgruntled petitioner had made a representation being aggrieved by the fallacy of allegations and frivolousness of litigation initiated by the complainant and in the said representation it is averred that the complainant is already married to one Anurag Upadhyay and has 20-year-old daughter.
She has been blackmailing the petitioner and extorting money and the petitioner has already paid Rs.4 lakh to her.

Focusing on the insatiable greed of complainant, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that earlier also, she made a complaint and after taking money from the petitioner, she gave an affidavit before the Director General of Police for taking her complaint back and now she is demanding Rs.25 Lakh and when petitioner refused to fulfill her illegitimate lust of ill-gotten wealth, she lodged the FIR.
Copy of the representation dated 17.08.2022 made to Superintendent of Police, Narsinghpur is made appendage to this petition.

5. Shri Kochar submitted that under the existing circumstances, it is clear that the petitioner has been fallaciously implicated in the alleged offence and even otherwise, if the allegations made by the complainant in FIR are considered to be true on their face value, even then offence under Section 376 of IPC is not made out.
6.

In rebuttal, learned counsel for the State and also the learned counsel for the complainant have opposed the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner and submitted that the allegations made in the complaint are true or untrue can only be ascertained after the trial is conducted and unless the evidence is recorded, it is arduous to believe whether those allegations are correct or incorrect and the petitioner has committed any crime or not.
According to them, this is not a proper stage where FIR and subsequent proceedings can be quashed only on the basis of material available before this Court.

7. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the rival parties and perusal of the record, especially the contents of FIR, indubitably, it is clear that the petitioner stayed with complainant at her rented house and developed physical relation with her.
The relationship between them continued for long time.
The complainant is aged 40 years; a married lady and has a girl aged 20 years out of first wedlock, knowing fully well that the petitioner is also a married man.
Thus, it is inscrutable to comprehend as to how promise of marriage can be given or accepted by them especially when the prosecutrix's first marriage still subsists.
Not only she, but the petitioner is also not in a position to marry with her unless his first marriage is dissolved.

The complainant has also made a complaint to the police and then submitted affidavit that the petitioner did not commit any crime nor developed physical relation but she made false allegations against him and thus on affidavit she withdrew the complaint made against the petitioner.

It is apposite here to go-through the legal position already set at rest.

The Supreme Court in the case of Prashant Bharti v. State (NCT of Delhi)

sentences.text: It is relevant to notice, that she had alleged, that she was induced into a physical relationship by Prashant Bharti, on the assurance that he would marry her.
Obviously, an inducement for marriage is understandable if the same is made to an unmarried person.
The judgment and decree dated 23.9.2008 reveals, that the complainant/prosecuterix was married to Lalji Porwal on 14.6.2003.

It also reveals,
that the aforesaid marriage subsisted till 23.9.2008, when the two divorced one another by mutual consent under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act.

In her supplementary statement dated 21.2.2007, the complainant/prosecuterix accused Prashant Bhati of having had physical relations with her on 23.12.2006, 25.12.2006 and 1.1.2007 at his residence, on the basis of a false promise to marry her.
It is apparent from irrefutable evidence, that during the dates under reference and for a period of more than one year and eight months thereafter, she had remained married to Lalji Porwal.

In such a fact situation, the assertion made by the complainant/prosecuterix, that the appellant-accused had physical relations with her, on the assurance that he would marry her, is per se false and as such,
unacceptable.
She, more than anybody else, was clearly aware of the fact that she had a subsisting valid marriage with Lalji Porwal.
Accordingly, there was no question of anyone being in a position to induce her into a physical relationship under an assurance of marriage.

If the judgment and decree dated 23.9.2008 produced before us by the complainant/prosecuterix herself is taken into consideration alongwith the factual position depicted in the supplementary statement dated 21.2.2007, it would clearly emerge, that the complainant /prosecuterix was in a relationship of adultery on 23.12.2006, 25.12.2006 and 1.1.2007 with the appellant-accused, while she was validly married to her previous husband Lalji Porwal.

In the aforesaid view of the matter, we are satisfied that the assertion made by the complainant/prosecuterix,
that she was induced to a physical relationship by Prashant Bharti, the appellant-accused, on the basis of a promise to marry her, stands irrefutably falsified.

The High Court of Jharkhand, Ranchi in the case of Manish Kumar Sharma v. The State of Jharkhand passed in Cr.M.P. No.488/2022 considering the facts of the case, which are almost akin to the case at hand, has observed as under:-
"In view of the submissions of the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the parties,
the Court has gone through the materials on record and finds that admittedly the mother of this petitioner has filed the complaint case against the O.P.No.2 and thereafter the present case has been filed. Annexure-4 is the statement of the informant under section 164 Cr.P.C. in which in paragraph no.4 she has clearly stated that she was married with one Pradip Mandal and the case of divorce is going on which suggest that a married woman has established relationship with her consent with this petitioner.

sentences.text: The question remains that when two adult have established relationship particularly considering that the informant is a married woman, whether section 376(2)(n) IPC can be attracted or not?

In the case in hand, the victim who is a married woman voluntarily had sex with the petitioner, knowing that she cannot enter into marriage with the petitioner in view of the fact that she was a married woman.

Even assuming that promise by the petitioner for marriage, she was knowing that she is a married woman and marriage will not take place, and inspite of that she has established relationship with the petitioner that promise is illegal and that cannot be a basis for prosecution under section 376(2)(n) of the IPC.

In the case in hand,
there is no question that this petitioner has allured as she was already married and she was not divorced and inspite of that she has established the relationship with this petitioner.
Section 406 IPC is for punishment for breach of trust.
In order to bring criminal breach, to prove entrustment is an essential ingredient under section 405 IPC.
Section 420 IPC is only made out if from the very beginning the intention of cheat is there which is lacking in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
Thus, prima facie it appears that the ingredients of those sections are not made out.

The Court has gone through the order taking cognizance dated 24.09.2021 and finds that the learned court filled the words 'cognizance' and 'personal' in the blank space which suggest that there is non- application of judicial mind, and in that view of the matter, the order taking cognizance dated 24.09.2021 arising out of Deoghar Mahila P.S.Case No.6 of 2021, corresponding to G.R. No.1839 of 2021, pending before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Deoghar, is set aside, and the matter is remitted back to the learned concerned court to pass afresh order in accordance with law."
10.

(i) Prosecutrix was a married woman having three children.

sentences.text: (ii) Accused was staying in a tenanted premises situated in front of the house of the prosecutrix.

(iii) Though initially hesitant, the prosecutrix developed liking for the accused, and both started having sexual relationship with each other.
(iv) The prosecutrix delivered a male child on 28/10/2011 from the loin of the accused.
(v) The prosecutrix went to the native place of the accused in 2012 and came to know that he was a married man having children.
(vi) The prosecutrix still continued to live with the accused in separate premises.
(vii) The prosecutrix and her husband took divorce by mutual consent in 2014 and thereafter prosecutrix permanently left her three children with her husband.

(viii) The prosecutrix lodged the complaint on 21 st March, 2015 alleging that she had consented for sexual relationship with the accused as the accused had promised her to marry and subsequently did not marry.

21. In the instant case, the prosecutrix who herself was a married woman having three children,
could not be said to have acted under the alleged false promise given by the appellant or under the misconception of fact while giving the consent to have sexual relationship with the appellant.
Undisputedly, she continued to have such relationship with him at least for about five years till she gave complaint in the year 2015.

Even if the allegations made by her in her deposition before the court, are taken on their face value, then also to construe such allegations as 'rape' by the appellant,
would be stretching the case too far.

The prosecutrix being a married woman and the mother of three children was matured and intelligent enough to understand the significance and the consequences of the moral or immoral quality of act she was consenting to.

Even otherwise, if her entire conduct during the course of such relationship with the accused, is closely seen, it appears that she had betrayed her husband and three children by having relationship with the accused, for whom she had developed liking for him.
She had gone to stay with him during the subsistence of her marriage with her husband, to live a better life with the accused.

Till the time she was impregnated by the accused in the year 2011, and she gave birth to a male child through the loin of the accused,
she did not have any complaint against the accused of he having given false promise to marry her or having cheated her.

She also visited the native place of the accused in the year 2012 and came to know that he was a married man having children also, still she continued to live with the accused at another premises without any grievance.
She even obtained divorce from her husband by mutual consent in 2014, leaving her three children with her husband.
It was only in the year 2015 when some disputes must have taken place between them, that she filed the present complaint.
The accused in his further statement recorded under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. had stated that she had filed the complaint as he refused to fulfill her demand to pay her huge amount.

Thus, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, it could not be said by any stretch of imagination that the Amitabh Pratap Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67308039/
6 prosecutrix had given her consent for the sexual relationship with the appellant under the misconception of fact, so as to hold the appellant guilty of having committed rape within the meaning of Section 375 of IPC."

sentences.text: Based on the holistic consideration of the facts and circumstances summarised in the foregoing paragraphs and the judicial conscience, I do not hesitate to exercise the inherent powers vested under Section 482 of CrPC.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

Thus, FIR registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, Narsingpur vide Crime No.51/2022 on the fulcrum of a complaint made by respondent No.2 against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n),
328, 506, 420 of the Indian Penal Code is hereby quashed.
Consequently, the impugned order dated 11.09.2023 passed in S.T.No.29/2023 is also set aside.
12. Before parting with the case, it needs to be emphasized that all subsequent proceedings pursuant to said FIR, will automatically come to an end.
13. The petition stands allowed.
(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE sudesh SUDESH KUMAR SHUKLA 2024.03.14
